hints: Look first at the shape and position of the absorption above 3000 wavenumbers, as this tells you about O-H and N-H bonds.
Notice there is a broad, rounded dip centred around 3300 cm-1 but no strong sharp dip around 1700 cm-1 for C=O.
Connect a broad alcohol O-H with no carbonyl to decide which functional group family P must belong to.
walkthrough:
**Read the spectrum like a detective**

Remember, in IR a dip downwards means absorption. Look for the two key regions: O-H / N-H around 2500 to 3500 cm-1, and C=O around 1680 to 1750 cm-1.

Key regions:
$$\text{O-H (alcohol): broad } 3200-3600 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$
$$\text{C=O: strong sharp } 1680-1750 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$

**Spot the broad O-H peak**

The spectrum shows a very broad, strong absorption centred at about 3350 cm-1. That broad rounded shape is classic for hydrogen bonding.

This tells us P contains an $\text{O-H}$ group involved in hydrogen bonding, as in an alcohol.

**Check for a carbonyl group**

Now look around 1700 cm-1. The trace is flat and high (high transmittance) there, so there is no $\text{C=O}$ absorption.

That rules out any ester, aldehyde, ketone or carboxylic acid, all of which need a strong C=O peak.

**Match to the options**

Only propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, has an alcohol O-H but no C=O. It also shows $\text{C-H}$ absorptions just below 3000 cm-1 and $\text{C-O}$ around 1100 cm-1, which fit the spectrum.

So P must be the alcohol.

options.A: Methyl ethanoate is an ester, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_3$. It must show a strong sharp C=O peak around 1740 cm-1 and no broad O-H peak. The spectrum has the opposite pattern, broad O-H and no C=O.
options.B: Propanal is an aldehyde, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$. It must show a strong C=O peak around 1720 cm-1 plus aldehydic C-H peaks. The spectrum shows no C=O peak, so this is ruled out.
options.C: Propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, has both C=O and O-H. Its O-H is extremely broad, covering 2500 to 3300 cm-1 and overlapping C-H, plus a strong C=O around 1710 cm-1. Here the broad peak is narrower and centred higher, and the C=O peak is missing.
options.D: Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHOH}$. The broad absorption around 3350 cm-1 is the hydrogen-bonded O-H stretch, the sharp dips near 2950 cm-1 are C-H stretches, and there is correctly no C=O absorption near 1700 cm-1.
